events.text: You have walked a long way on very careful feet, and you have got used to sages. But here is a house with no child, and its dreams lie out on the night like washing, and you have begun stepping through them on your way past. A dream has grass in it. You stop with one hoof up. Does it count? The old books do not say. A qilin walked into a dream once, and a child came of it. That much they do say.

choices.text: Put the hoof down, gently, and see who is sleeping

effects.log: Nothing bends that you can see. You are at the back of someone's sleep, in a room swept for nobody. Nothing has been harmed. You go on telling yourself that, quite carefully.

choices.text: Go round. A sleeper is a living thing too

effects.log: You walk round by the high road. It takes a long while, and there is nobody on it. You have kept your feet clean, and you have kept them to yourself.

events.text: A farmer's dream, the first you stay in: he has been carrying one bucket up one hill for twenty years, and it has a hole, and there is no child at the top. You stand beside the path. Dream grass grows thick there, every blade of it just as he remembers grass. You work out where the gaps are. He wakes in the morning and tells nobody, and you are still out in the field of it on three legs.

choices.text: Stay till the gaps come clear

effects.log: It takes till the next new moon. By then you know how to go through a person's sleep and leave no track. He never sees you. He has a slightly better year with the bucket.

choices.text: Walk straight out. It is only a dream

effects.log: It is only a dream. There is a line of bent blades behind you in the shape of your hooves. He wakes with a headache and kicks the dog, and that is only a morning.

events.text: Two mornings later the whole well knows. A woman down the lane dreamed of a great beast with a shining hide, and she tells it over her washing. They go into it carefully. It was fat, was it? Then it was a pig. A pig is money. You stand on the hill and hear this. That afternoon her house sells its good pot to buy a sow. You have carried the words of sages to the doors of kings.

choices.text: Go back in, and stand where she can see the horn

effects.log: She looks at it for a long time. In the morning she says it was a very big pig. But she keeps the sow, and she has started looking at the sky.

choices.text: Leave it. A sow will do that house no harm

effects.log: It does not. The sow farrows nine. It is the most successful thing you have done in a century, and none of the sages ever came to as much.

events.text: An older sister dreams of you in a house by the river, and tells it at breakfast. Her younger sister goes quiet, and then says she will buy it. A silk skirt, for one dream. It is an old trick: a girl did that in Silla, they say, and her son was a king. The older sister laughs and takes the skirt. You are on the hill, and you did not know that you could be sold. You do not feel any different.

choices.text: Walk in the sleep of the one who paid

effects.log: She is a sharp, frightened girl, dreaming hard on purpose, with her eyes shut, looking for you. You stand a long way off and let her not find you. It seems the honest thing. She marries well anyway.

choices.text: Walk in the sleep of the one who sold

effects.log: She dreams of the skirt, and she is quite happy. You stay a while for the pleasure of it, and you go on your way wondering about the price of you, which is not high.

events.text: You are halfway across a sleep, in a bean field that does not exist, when the sleeper turns round. Nobody turns round. {npc} looks at you, and at your hoof, which you are holding up, and at the beans. "You can't put it there," {he} says. "I planted those." {He} fetches a broom, and sweeps a strip down the rows to the bare dirt, as wide as a hoof, and goes back to work. Nobody in any dream has ever made room for you.

choices.text: Walk down the path

effects.log: It holds. You go down it to the end, and out. The next night it is there again, with a little more swept, and {he} is sitting at the far end of it with nothing to say.

choices.text: Step out of that sleep, and take the long way round the valley

effects.log: You lie on the hill, knowing that down there someone goes on sweeping a strip of dirt, night after night, for a visitor. It stops at harvest. It is very quiet in the beans.

events.text: You come again. The path has stones in it now, laid flat. {npc} has made a place to sit, though {he} knows you cannot, and {he} uses it. You have no voice in here, so {he} talks. Years of trying at this house, and everybody has told {him} what to ask you for: a son, a clever one. "I am not going to ask you for anything," {he} says. "It is nice to have somebody stand still. Look at you. Is it hard?"

choices.text: Lower your head, to say that it is

effects.log: {He} laughs, and tells you about {his} bad back in reply, and {he} is very good at it. You stay until the dream goes grey. {He} sweeps up after you, though there is nothing to sweep.

choices.text: Go on standing. It is the only thing you have ever said

effects.log: {He} nods, and you stand, and {he} talks about the neighbours. That is all that happens. Out on the hill at dawn you are surprised at how much of your strength it took.

events.text: You go and look at {npc} awake, from the hill. It was a mistake, or else it was not. {He} has chapped hands, a voice for the ox that you have not heard in the dream, and a stick. {He} walks straight across the ant road by the gate, thinking about something, and does not look. That night you come down the swept path, and {he} moves over on the stone, and asks why you are standing so far off.

choices.text: Come back to the stones

effects.log: You come back. That foot is out there in the world, on the ants, every morning. You have stood beside kings for less. It is possible, you find, to know this and to stand here.

choices.text: Stay where you are, at the far end, this once

effects.log: {He} looks at you across the beans. You have no way to tell {him}. {He} does not sweep that night. In the morning you watch the gate from the hill as {he} goes over the ants again, and you count them.

events.text: {npc} has a length of cord in the dream, the kind that is tied at a birth. {He} holds it out as far as {his} arm goes, and stops. "I know you do not come into a house," {he} says. "I know you can't touch me; you would have by now. I will raise whatever comes. You will never come in at the door. Nobody will marry us, and it is only a dream, and I would like to have said it." Your horn is a long way from {his} hand.

choices.text: Lower your horn, until it is as near as it can be

effects.log: There is the width of a bean leaf between them. {He} ties the cord in the air, right there, and it stays. It is a very bad knot. You carry the look of it out of that sleep, and up the hill.

choices.text: Lift your head. A vow is a thing that steps on someone

effects.log: You step back on the path, and walk it to the end. In the morning {he} tells the cooking pot that {he} dreamed of nothing. {He} is a very poor liar, even to pots.

events.text: You know this house from the inside of its nights now. The rent comes as a red bull. The old woman of the house comes as a flight of stairs. The leak in the east room is the sea. Every morning, from the hill, you see {npc} get up and go out and do something about the bull, with a stick and a basket. You cannot help with it. All you can do is stand next to the bull.

choices.text: Stand next to the bull

effects.log: It is a big, stupid, worried animal. {npc} comes and stands with you, in {his} sleep, and the two of you look at it. That year it does not charge until the autumn.

choices.text: Move on through, to the sea in the east room

effects.log: You wade in, carefully; a lot is alive in it. It goes on leaking, awake. But {he} has started to dream of that room with a beast in it up to the knees, and {he} finds {he} can sleep through the sound.

events.text: {npc}'s dreams have gone thin this winter. There is nothing in the beans, and the path comes and goes. Awake, down there, there is a fever in the house, and no money for a physician. The herb it wants is on the ridge behind you, right under your nose. To pick it is a blade broken. {He} sits on the stones, very small, and asks if you would mind standing a little nearer.

choices.text: Stand nearer, all the nights of it

effects.log: {He} comes through in the spring, with no help from you. You have stood in one sleep for forty nights without moving a hoof. {He} tells the pot that someone sat up with {him}. {He} has the wrong idea about that, and the right one.

choices.text: Bite off the herb, and leave it on the gatepost

effects.log: One blade. It comes away with a small sound that you hear all the way down the hill. They boil it, and it may even help. You go back up with a bitter taste that is not the herb.

events.text: The well has it, and then the district. A rich house in the county town has sent a woman with an offer: a dream like that can be sold, as they did in Silla, if it is told properly and paid for. A year's rice, and {npc} says in front of witnesses that the dream belongs to them now. {He} has not eaten well since the rent. That night {he} is on the stones with {his} chin on {his} knees. "Would you even know?" {he} asks.

choices.text: Stay on the path as ever, and let {him} settle it

effects.log: {He} settles it. You do not learn how till spring, when the roof is mended, and the swept path is still there every night, with one stone missing. You have never asked about the stone.

choices.text: Go over to the rich house that night, and see what wants buying

effects.log: There is a young wife lying awake there, very much afraid. You stand a while, and nobody has swept anything for you. You come back angry with no one, which is not at all like being at peace.

events.text: Broad daylight. The landlord's man has come to the gate about the rent, with two others, and {npc} is saying something, and now {he} is on the ground. You are on the hill. You could be in that yard in four breaths, a thing the size of a barn, with a horn. Between you and the gate is half a li of spring barley. You have never once put your foot on anything. You can hear the stick from here.

choices.text: Stand still. Afterwards, go into {his} sleep, and stand where {he} can see what you did

effects.log: {He} looks at you across the beans with {his} one good eye. "You watched," {he} says. You lower your head. {He} has a long think. "Yes," {he} says. "Well. I told you that I knew." It is the worst night of your life.

choices.text: Go down. Through the barley, all of it, at a run

effects.log: They see you coming and they run, and nobody is ever sure what they saw. There is a track through the barley as wide as an ox cart. That is a winter's food, for the house you came to save. {He} sees it from the mat, and says nothing.

choices.text: Turn round and walk away over the ridge. You cannot do this

effects.log: You walk till the sound has gone, and then for a month. The old books call you the benevolent beast. They do not say what it is for. You do not go back to the beans.

events.text: Snow. {npc} went out for the strayed ox and did not come back, and of course you have found {him}: ten paces off, in a drift. {He} has sat down, as they do, and is going to sleep. It is quite warm, then. So {he} comes to the stones in {his} dream, pleased to see you, and will not wake. You have no voice and no hands. The only loud thing in that dream is what would happen if you stamped.

choices.text: Stamp. Go down the path at a gallop, and break it all

effects.log: The stones, the beans, every row {he} ever swept. It comes apart like a plate. {He} wakes choking in the drift, furious and alive, and crawls home. {He} knows who did that. {He} starts again in spring, with the first stone.

choices.text: Stand still, as you have always stood

effects.log: A woodcutter finds {him} at first light, and it costs {him} two fingers and most of that winter. {He} comes back to the stones in spring with the broom held oddly. {He} asks you nothing, and you do not know if you have won.

choices.text: Get out of the dream. Get out of all of it

effects.log: You leave {him} to the woodcutter. You are nine valleys away before you can bear to find out that there was one. You do not walk in that sleep again.

events.text: The house has a child, when everybody had stopped asking. It is called {bk_child} at the naming, before the lane, and {npc} stands up and tells it: the beans, the hoof, the five colours. It has got to five colours, and you were not consulted. You are on the hill. You have not touched anyone in this house, ever, and you will not. A small wet noise is coming from the back room. You have never heard anything so loud.

choices.text: Walk in that night, and look into the baby's sleep

effects.log: There is nothing in there yet, only warm, and a very large feeling about milk. There is room in it for one hoof, and you do not use it. You stand at the door of it until it is light.

choices.text: Stay on the hill. It will have enough looking at it

effects.log: The whole lane comes to see the qilin-child, and to remark on its forehead. You watch from far up. You are the only one in the county who has not said that it is clever.

events.text: A second, called {bk_child}, and this time the house tells it with an eye on the neighbours. {npc} is on the stones, rocking. "They want to know what you did for this one," {he} says. "Was it a small hoof, or what? They have got a fortune-teller in." You know about spitting out a book of jade for such a child; everyone does. You have nothing in your mouth. You have four feet, and you have brought them.

choices.text: Stand where the baby's sleep can find you, small and plain

effects.log: It is the same warm, the same milk. {npc} tells them the dream was a small one, and {he} says it proudly. The fortune-teller takes a look, goes home, and gives the money back.

choices.text: Go out on a clear night, and stand on the ridge where they can say they saw you

effects.log: Half the lane sees you go along it under the moon. There is a good deal of talk. {bk_child} has a second story to live under now, and a bigger one. You had not thought that through.

events.text: {bk_child} is seven, was meant to be a sage, and has just hit a neighbour's boy with a spade. {bk_child} can't read the Thousand Characters, and stamps on anything that crawls, with joy. The house still tells the dream at the new year, looks at {bk_child}, and then looks at the ceiling. {bk_love} tells you on the stones, laughing a little. Then not laughing. That is a long life to spend disappointing a dream.

choices.text: Go into {bk_love}'s sleep, and be smaller

effects.log: You stand there in the beans, about the size of a goat. {bk_love} looks at you a long while, and the next new year tells it differently: a small, plain beast that only stopped to look. The child eats through the whole story.

choices.text: Leave it. They will get used to the spade

effects.log: They do not. But the child gets used to the ceiling, learns a trade, and laughs loudly. You stand on the hill to hear it, some evenings. You have seen sages do worse.

events.text: At seven, {bk_child} has not come home, and it is raining, and the whole house is out with lanterns. You have known for hours. On the dyke path a small figure is standing on one foot. The ants have come up out of the wet, all over the path, and there is nowhere to put the other one. {bk_child} has been there since dusk, soaked, wobbling, crying a bit. {bk_love} gets there at last. "Why didn't you just step?"

choices.text: Stand on the dyke, in the lantern light, on three legs

effects.log: {bk_child} looks up and across, straight at you, awake, as nobody ever has. {bk_love} sees it too, lifts the child off the path, and does not ask again. It will be hit a great deal, that child. It has your feet. You stay until the ants have gone home.

choices.text: Stay out of the light. Let the child think that it is only a child

effects.log: {bk_love} carries it home. "There were ants," says {bk_child}, and is given soup. You stay out there all night in the rain. You know what it is going to be like, and how long it takes, and that you can do nothing about any of it.

events.text: {npc} comes down the stones very slowly now, with the broom, for the look of it. {His} hair has gone white in the dream too. You have been married to this, in a manner of speaking, for forty years. {He} sits. {He} looks at {his} hand and at your horn, which has been a bean leaf away from it all that time. "In here," {he} says. "Would it count?" You have been asking that since the first night.

choices.text: Close the gap. It is only a dream

effects.log: It is a very small thing. It is warm and dry, and rough across the knuckles, as you had thought. Nothing breaks. You stand on the hill at dawn, shaking. You do not know if anything has been bent. You have never felt better.

choices.text: Stay as you are. You have come this far

effects.log: {He} looks at the gap, and nods. "That is what I thought you would say," {he} says. "I would not have liked it, if you had. I would have liked it very much." {He} goes on sitting there, with {his} hand exactly where it was.

events.text: There is nobody there. You have come down the hill at the usual hour and stepped toward the usual sleep, and it is not there to step into. They took {bk_love} up the hill on the third day. You could see it well from where you were, across two fields. You have never been closer than that, and you are not going to be. You go on standing with one hoof up, where the first stone was.

choices.text: Walk to the grave by daylight, through the whole lane, by the road

effects.log: You have not walked by day in a hundred years. They come out of their doors, and nobody speaks. You stand beside the mound. The grass has been cut, and for once there is somewhere to put your feet.

choices.text: Go every night to where it was, and stand

effects.log: You go, and you go on going. Nothing is there. Sleepers in that village say, now and then, that they dreamed of a strip of swept earth, and they cannot say where.

events.text: Eighty years. You listen at their well. The dream is much better than it was: there was thunder, and the beast spoke in verse, and a book of jade as thick as a door. Every child of that line is told it at the new year, and then looked at. So far they have had three clerks, a midwife and a very bad poet. The latest, named for {bk_child}, has just been given the news, and has gone out to the shed.

choices.text: Go into that sleep in the shed, for one night, and just stand

effects.log: It is a tired young dream with a great many books in it, all shut. You stand beside them. In the morning the young one gets up looking a little less like a person who owes something.

choices.text: Let them have their thunder

effects.log: You walk on. The new year after that, there is a second book of jade. You have started to feel quite sorry for the first one.

events.text: One of {bk_child}'s people has come to the field-stone where the story says you stood: a thin scholar with a notebook. There was no qilin that year, the scholar has worked out, and no sage, and the old dreamer had a fever. It is a family vanity, and it ought to be said. The scholar sits down to write it. There is an ant crossing the page. The brush stops above the paper, and it stays there until the ant has gone.

choices.text: Show yourself on the ridge, at the edge of their eye

effects.log: The scholar looks up, and looks for a long time at nothing. The notebook goes on saying what it says. But there is a new line at the bottom now, in a smaller hand.

choices.text: Stay away. That was better than any proof

effects.log: You go. The book comes out, and it is quite right, and the house stops speaking to its author. You would like to tell someone about the ant. You have never had anyone to tell.

events.text: You have stood near no house for sixty years. {npc} does not sleep. {He} is the night watch at the grain store, and you cannot walk into a sleep {he} never gets round to, and one night {he} comes up the hill with a lantern to see what is standing there. {He} looks at how you stand. {He} looks down at {his} own big feet, and the grass. Then {he} takes off {his} straw shoes. Nobody has ever seen you awake, and stayed.

choices.text: Stay, and let {him} look

effects.log: You are poor company, and {he} is used to that. {He} comes up most nights, barefoot, and tells you what the rats did. {He} wants nothing from you that you can think of. You have begun to listen for the lantern.

choices.text: Go, while {he} is looking down

effects.log: {He} looks up, and there is a hill. {He} stays till morning anyway, in bare feet. Then {he} goes back to the rats, and you watch from very far off as {he} goes round the ant road.

events.text: A person is sitting on the ground by the ant road in your meadow, with a bruise on the jaw and no weapon. You do not know them. They do not look up. "They are crossing," they say, as one says it to somebody else waiting at a ford. You stand. They sit. The ants go by in the last of the light. "I was told it would be bigger," they say, and you do not know if they mean you, or the ants.

choices.text: Wait with them until the last ant is over

effects.log: It is well after dark. They stand up and stretch, and they cross the meadow, and they put their feet down just as you would, with no idea that they do it. Nobody has ever kept you company at this.

choices.text: Step into their next sleep, and see what they have made of it

effects.log: There is a swept strip down the middle of it. They could not tell you why. They have kept it up for years, and it goes nowhere, and you stand at the end of it for longer than you should.

events.text: You are six. They tell the dream at the new year, with you on a cushion, and then they ask you to recite. You can do the first line. A mosquito on your arm is filling up, and you watch it with interest. Your uncle slaps at it, and you feel it go, and you cry so hard that they fetch {npc}, the oldest friend this house has, who looks at you and at the smear, does not laugh, and takes you out to see the ants.

choices.text: Ask {npc} why it hurts

effects.log: "It is only that you felt it," says {npc}. "Most do not." {He} shows you where they go in, under the step. You are late for the recital. Everybody is very understanding, and that is not a good sign.

choices.text: Learn to look the other way when it happens

effects.log: You learn. There is a lot going on at table that you do not look at. You get the second line by spring, they give you a rice cake, and everyone is so relieved.

events.text: You are ten, and you cannot be hit. You do not know this until the boys behind the mill try it. You do not do anything. You just are not where it lands, by a little, over and over, until they are tired and very angry and go to fetch a bigger one. You could not hit back if you wanted to: your hands come up in red welts at the thought. {npc} puts vinegar on them and looks at you for a long time.

choices.text: Go back behind the mill tomorrow, and let them try

effects.log: They try for a month. Then they grow bored, and start bringing you their troubles. You are still no good at anything, and there is not one mark on you.

choices.text: Stand still next time, and take one, so that they will stop

effects.log: You stand still. It hurts a great deal, and it is over quickly, and they go off satisfied. You have learned how to lose a fight so that everyone feels better.

events.text: You are fourteen. The county schoolmaster has come four days on a mule to examine the qilin-child, and the whole house has gone into debt for the chicken. The man asks you about the Analects. You know a fair amount, and no more than that. You can see it happen on that face. A kind man. Behind the man, on the wall, {npc} is eating a piece of the chicken. {He} looks at you, and shrugs.

choices.text: Tell the schoolmaster plainly that you are no sage, and that the chicken was a friend of yours

effects.log: The schoolmaster laughs so hard that the cup has to go down. It is all over the county by the new year. The house does not speak to you for a month, and for the first time in years you are breathing.

choices.text: Say what is wanted, and eat the chicken

effects.log: You get through it by watching the eyebrows, and you keep down the chicken till the mule has gone. The schoolmaster writes them a very good letter. They hang it on the wall, where you can see it from your bed.

events.text: Your sixteenth year. An old monk has been teaching the village boys to breathe, and they have been at the first gate for years, red in the face. You sit down to rest, nod off, and dream of a hoof coming down, very slowly, where there is room. You wake on the far side of the gate. The yard has stopped to look. {npc} takes you by the sleeve. "Come away," {he} says. "I will tell you what this house dreamed."

choices.text: Hear all of it

effects.log: A swept path. {bk_anc}, who would not put a foot down. {bk_line}, born to a house that told it wrong from the first day. "It never touched any of them," {npc} says. "That is what you come from. Now you know how much to expect."

choices.text: Say that you only fell asleep

effects.log: {npc} looks at you, and lets go of your sleeve. "As you like," {he} says. You go back and do the breathing with the others, red in the face, for the look of it. You are not good at that either.

events.text: There is a sword school in the county town, and the house has borrowed for it. You last eleven days. You have the best footwork the teacher has ever seen, and when it comes to the cut, your arm swells to the elbow and you faint. A boy of twelve has just put you on the floor, twice, and is worried. You also went through their third gate last week, by accident, on a bench. {npc} has come to fetch you home, with a cart.

choices.text: Stay on, sweep the yard, and learn to get out of the way

effects.log: You stay a year. They send their worst students to you, to see how it is done. Nobody can touch you, you have never once been a danger to anyone, and they are not sure what to write on the letter.

choices.text: Go home on the cart. Say it was the food

effects.log: It was the food, you tell them, for some years. They are very kind about it. Your arm goes down by the second week, and you are sick with shame and quite well.

events.text: Two villages have fallen out over water, and they have met at the sluice with hoes. You happened to be passing. You do not remember deciding anything. You are standing in the middle of it in your good jacket, with your arm swelling, and you are not where any of the hoes come down. It is going on a long time. Someone is going to be killed, and not you. {npc} is at the top of the bank, shouting something.

choices.text: Stay in the middle until they are too tired to lift them

effects.log: It takes from noon till dusk. Nobody is dead. They go home hating you, in both villages, for reasons they can't quite name. In a year or two they have begun to send for you when the water is low.

choices.text: Get out, and fetch the headmen

effects.log: It is the sensible thing, and you run very well. By the time they come, there are two men who will not walk again, and no one says that you should have done anything else. You sleep very badly.

events.text: People come to you now from far off, when they have no child. They do not quite say why. They ask if they might sleep at your gate. The story has got out that you are some sort of luck. A couple nineteen years married are out there now on a straw mat in the frost. You have no idea what you could do. {npc} brings out a second blanket, and looks at you as {he} goes by.

choices.text: Sit up with them, and tell them the truth: you have nothing

effects.log: They are very polite. You all sit up anyway. In the small hours one of them falls asleep on your shoulder, and you hold quite still, which you are good at. You hear, a year later, that they have taken in a niece.

choices.text: Say that you will do what you can, and send them home hopeful

effects.log: They go away so happy. It is not even a lie; you have done what you can. You hear nothing about them after that, and you do not ask.

events.text: {npc} has just been insulted at the market, to {his} face, over a debt you owe. You stood there, with your arm swelling, and you said something mild. {He} walks home ahead of you, quickly, with the basket. At home {he} bangs down a pot. "Do you know what it is," {he} says, "to be married to someone who will never hit anyone for you?" {He} turns. "Do you know what it is when I want you to?"

choices.text: Tell {him} about the dream, and the hill, and how long a thing can stand and watch

effects.log: {He} sits down on the floor with the pot. "It stood on a hill," {he} says. You nod. "And let them." You nod. It takes {him} about a year. One night you wake, and there is a broom by the bed, and you know what it means.

choices.text: Go and pay the debt, with what you have got

effects.log: It is not what {he} asked. {He} knows it, and you know it. Nobody at the market says anything after that. {He} looks at you across the pot, and {he} does not ask again.

events.text: {npc} has come home with a split lip, and will not say who. You find out: a bigger child has been taking things, and today {he} stopped it, with a stone. {He} is rather proud. {His} knuckles are not swollen. {He} walks across the ants at the step without a glance. You stand there with the vinegar in your hand, and you cannot think what it is that you are feeling.

choices.text: Ask {him} to show you how {he} did it

effects.log: {He} shows you, with a lot of noise. You are hopeless. {He} laughs so hard that {he} has to sit down, and the lip starts again. You tell {him} what the house dreamed, and {he} has no interest. You could watch this for a long time.

choices.text: Take {him} out to the step, and show {him} where the ants go

effects.log: {He} looks, because you asked. {He} is a good-natured child, and {he} puts {his} foot down more carefully for a week or so. You do not know if you have given {him} something or taken it.

events.text: {npc} finds you on the road: a very good swordsman, with very tired eyes, who has not come to kill anyone. {He} has a child at home wasting away, and a physician who has told {him} about the blood of the beast that harms nothing. It would only want a cup. {He} knows about you, and about the arm. {He} is asking first. {He} has a clean cup with {him}, wrapped up in a cloth.

choices.text: Refuse {him}, by hand, and take the swelling

ok.log: It is the first blow you have ever landed. {He} goes down more from surprise than anything. You are ill for a month with an arm like a bolster, and you hear {his} cart going away, slowly, with an empty cup.

fail.log: You are not where the first cut lands, and you are where the second does. {He} fills {his} cup, binds you up, and thanks you, and means it. You lie in the road, not sure that you would have said no.

choices.text: Hold out your arm. It is only a cup

effects.log: It does not even hurt much. {He} bows to you on the road, very low, with the cup held level, and walks away like someone carrying a full bowl across ice. You feel that you have done the right thing, for once.

events.text: {npc} again, on the same road, with the same cup. Twelve years. {He} has got old. "I got my cup, one way or another," {he} says. "It did nothing. The child died in the spring. I have gone on hunting you, I find, to see what you are for." {He} lays {his} sword on the ground, and picks it up again. "What you come from stood on a hill and watched, and was called kind. Hit me, one time. Or I will go and find {bk_anc}."

choices.text: Hit {him}, as hard as you can

ok.log: It is easy, and it is the worst thing you have ever felt. {He} lies there looking up, almost relieved. "So that is what you are," {he} says. Your hand never does go down all the way. You do not see {him} again.

fail.log: {He} has wanted this for twelve years, and you are a beginner. You wake in a ditch with your whole side on fire. The cup is standing on a stone beside you, full of clean water, and you do not know what it means.

choices.text: Sit down in the road, and stay sitting, whatever {he} does

effects.log: {He} stands over you until the sun has moved. {He} does not do it. In the end {he} sits down too, across the road, with the sword on {his} knees. At dusk you ask what the child was called, and {he} tells you.

events.text: You have started to wake up knowing things. That your neighbour has been dreaming of the sea. That the miller is afraid of a flight of stairs. You lie down, and you find that you are standing in somebody's sleep with one foot up, being very careful, and you can feel how thin the floor is. {npc} says that it is a road, and it goes on to a meadow. You could put the foot down. You could also drink.

choices.text: Put the foot down, and go on

effects.log: It is a long way across the sleep of this district, and everyone is in it. By morning you are more tired than you have ever been, and you know the way back. That is what frightens {npc}.

choices.text: Drink before bed, and forget what you saw

effects.log: It works. A season of it, and you remember nothing. You wake up thick and cheerful, you tread on what there is, and nobody has to be careful of you at all.

events.text: There is a war on the northern border, and the levy has come to the district. It is your turn. The officer hands you a spear. Your whole arm has come up before your fingers close, and the officer looks at it with no interest. A long way off to the north, the grass is being walked over by forty thousand feet, and you can feel it in your soles. {npc} says that they hang people for this. {He} has brought your coat.

choices.text: Put down the spear, in front of them all, and walk home

effects.log: They beat you, not very seriously, and you are not where most of it lands. They make you a litter-bearer instead. You carry what comes back for two years, and you do not drop anything. You are different after.

choices.text: Take it, and go with them, swollen, and hope not to use it

effects.log: You march. You do not have to, as it happens, or not in any way you can remember. You come home with the arm down, and the grass gone quiet in your sleep. That is what frightens you.

events.text: {npc} walks you up to an old field-stone, out past anyone's fields, and tells you to lie down with your head on it. It is cold. You sleep. In the dream you are lying just there, on the same stone, and something very large is standing beside you, trying not to wake you. It has been doing this for years; you can tell by how it stands. One hoof is up. {bk_anc} has the oldest eyes that you have seen in anything.

choices.text: Stay asleep. Let it stand

effects.log: You lie there, and it stands there. Nothing happens for what feels like thirty years. When you wake, the hard place in your chest that you have had since you were six has got some room in it.

choices.text: Get up, and ask it why it let them

effects.log: You have no voice in here. You find that you are shouting anyway. It stays exactly where it is and lowers its head, and that is the whole of what it has to say, and it is a great deal. You wake with a wet face.

events.text: You are sent for. You know the day, and you know the hill. There is a flat stone up there with four hoofmarks in it, worn deep, and all around it the grass stands as if it had never been looked at. At the foot of the stone lies a broom, worn down to the binding. Nobody has been up here in a hundred years. {npc} sees it, and {his} mouth opens. There is a second thing, a bit of cord with a very bad knot.

choices.text: Take the broom

effects.log: It weighs nothing, and it would not sweep a step. You go home with it under your arm. In the morning you find that you are looking at the floor of your house, and at who has to walk there.

choices.text: Take the cord, and try to undo it

effects.log: It cannot be done. You have good hands, and you sit up with it all night. Whoever tied that knot did not know how, and meant it. You tie it to your belt, and it never comes off.

events.text: You cannot hit and you cannot rest, and all night you stand in everyone's sleep. {npc} sits with you on the step. "You could lie down at the stone," {he} says, "and not wake, and walk on soft feet for as long as there is grass. Or tell them all it was a pig. It was always a pig. Step on the ants, once, on purpose, and it may let you go." {He} looks at the ants. "There is a road between. I have only heard of it."

choices.text: Tell them it was a pig. Put your foot down

effects.log: You do it at the new year, in front of everyone, and they are scandalised. Afterwards you go out on the step and put your foot down. Your arm does not swell. Nothing happens, and that is what happens.

choices.text: Lie down at the stone

effects.log: You lie down. In the morning there is nobody on the stone. There is something on the far side of the field, very careful with its feet, that does not look round.

choices.text: Stay awake and asleep both. Go on sweeping

effects.log: You put your foot down nowhere you have not looked. You go in by night and come home by day, with an arm like a bolster and a house to run. {npc} says someone once stood a long way off for this.

events.text: You hit a man today. It was a small dispute about a wall, and you hit the man in the ear, badly. Your arm stayed the size of an arm. The man hit you back, and you were exactly where it landed. You sit down in the road with your nose running, and you have never been so interested in anything. {npc} comes to fetch you home, and asks if you intend to go on like this.

choices.text: Go on for a bit. You have a lot to catch up on

effects.log: You lose every fight you are in for about three years. You have a wonderful time. Then it stops being interesting, and you go back to minding the wall, with some very ordinary bruises.

choices.text: Go out and look at the ants, to see if you still feel it

effects.log: You look. They are ants. They go in under the step. You stay a long time, trying, and you are not sure that it is nothing. You are not sure of anything any more, which is how most people live, you hear.

events.text: There is grass here that has never been trodden, and you go over it, and it stays. You have four soft feet and no opinions about walls. Some nights you go down and stand in the sleep of your old house. You know where they keep everything. You know who is worried. {npc} is dreaming of you tonight, and {he} has put out a bowl, in the dream, as if you would eat.

choices.text: Stand by the bowl

effects.log: {He} nods to you across the room, and goes back to what {he} was doing. They tell it at the well next morning, with a number of improvements. You are quite a lot bigger than you were.

choices.text: Go on up to the meadow, and do not go down again

effects.log: It is very clean up there, and you have no debts to anybody. There is an ant road across the high meadow. You stand and look at it, some evenings, the way one looks at a letter.

events.text: You have become a sort of custom. Houses with no child send for you, quietly. You sleep a night on their floor, stand in their dream, and do nothing at all, very well. In the morning you have breakfast and take what they give you, which is often a hen, and then you have to keep it. You have eleven hens. {npc} calls you the only sage in the province ever to be paid in poultry.

choices.text: Go when they send, for as long as you have feet

effects.log: Some of them have children after that. Most of them do not. They all say that they slept better, and they send more hens, and one of the hens has begun to follow you.

choices.text: Keep one night in each month for your own house

effects.log: You lie down there with no one to stand beside. {npc} says you snore. It is the first dream of your own you have had for years, and you cannot remember a thing about it.

events.text: They are telling the dream to a new child tonight. They think you are asleep. There is a lightning storm in it now, and the beast has given someone's great-grandfather a sword. A sword. You lie very still. {npc}, by the fire, looks across at you, and sees that your eyes are open, and that you are going red in the face. "Would you care to correct them?" {he} says, loudly, and the whole room turns round.

choices.text: Correct them. It was beans

effects.log: You tell it from the bed, in a voice like a dry leaf. It is a very short story. Nobody does anything in it. The new child looks at you in utter disappointment, and then asks what kind of beans.

choices.text: Say that there was a sword, and it was a very large one

effects.log: The room is delighted. You are asked about the sword for the rest of your days, and you improve it. It is the only weapon you have ever had any use for.

events.text: You ask to be carried out to the step this last autumn. There is a long discussion about where to put the mat. You keep sending them back. They do not know what you want, until the smallest one gets down on hands and knees and has a look. "There are ants," that one says. There are. Nobody else has ever said it. {npc} straightens the blanket, and they all stand holding your mat in the air, and they wait.

choices.text: Let them wait, until the road has gone by

effects.log: It takes most of the morning. Nobody puts you down. They are big, tired people, and their arms are shaking, and they do not ask. It is more than you would have thought of, and you have thought about this for a long time.

choices.text: Tell them to put you down a little to the right. There is a gap

effects.log: They set you down exactly there. Nothing bends. You lie in the sun with the road going by a hand's breadth from your ear, and the smallest one lies down on the other side, and listens too.
